items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: Kerry was the cause when I got into the band... So that's how he come to see that I had to get in the band.

ctx.x: Oh, if I can think of all of them, I should give them to you. Let me see which one I could name first. That was, because that time I was playing solo alto when I first started with them. Oh, your first instrument was solo alto? Solo alto. Because for the simple fact, they didn't have no trumpet for me. You see, Kerry was the cause when I got into the band, you see. Because my father, he didn't want me to go into the band, but Kerry claimed that I was doing so well, when my father would go away I'd take his…

Were there any white musicians that were involved studying with Mr. Kerry and someone like this? Or did he just, he worked entirely with the Negro people? That's right. That's right. That's perfectly amazing. That's right.

Because they had only one band here that was really playing music then, that was the Brobridge band. Yeah. That was Belle Melençon and them, Jean Fourjeau and them, Dr. Fourjeau and all of them. They used to have, oh they had a wonderful band, but that was a regular brass band. But they used to use a few pieces and go around playing like that during the time they had election and things like that. But they had a good band.
